messages:
ashley (acct-exec): FYI POC customer reporting intermittent JSON.parse failures when using function-calling + json_mode (non-streaming). They pasted a raw response with trailing garbage. Model: redwood-medium-v1, streaming=false, they do aggressive client retries on 429/500. Can we triage?

sam (sales-engineer): Can you paste the raw HTTP payload including headers and whether they reuse connections (keep-alive)?

ashley (acct-exec): Sample:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"choices":[{"message":{"name":"extract","arguments":"{\"id\":123}"}}]}
--leftover--
```
They saw a 429 once with X-Request-Id: req_poc42.

tyler (ml-eng): If they retry on the same TCP connection while the server is finishing the previous response we can get concatenated bytes. Need request ids to map to worker logs and whether they use gzip/chunked.

prashant (infra): Ops-bot pull traces for req_poc42. Short interim mitigation: advise SDK-level de-dup or a tiny client sanitizer that extracts the first top-level JSON before JSON.parse.

ops-bot: Trace found: req_poc42 -> worker-7. Worker log at 2026-03-20T20:12:05Z contains WARN "stream-terminate: leftover-bytes". Related req req_poc43.

tyler (ml-eng): That WARN points to a stream flush bug. Plan: hotfix in worker shim to append an explicit delimiter for json_mode responses, unit tests and staging canary. Patch + tests ~2h, staging ~2h, canary 10% same day.

sam (sales-engineer): Customer also asked about pricing impact if they disable retries. Quick FAQ line?

prashant (infra): One-liner: aggressive retries can increase token costs roughly in proportion to retry rate (e.g., 10% retry => ~10% extra tokens). Using idempotency keys and SDK de-dup avoids duplicate billing.

ashley (acct-exec): I'll tell customer: interim sanitizer + pricing note, hotfix in staging today, canary tomorrow, schedule call at 16:00 PT. Will post raw payloads if they send more. :thumbsup:
